items.title: IAEA says Iran stored near-weapons-grade uranium underground

featured_image.name: IAEA chief says Iran could be enriching uranium within ...

items.description:
Some of Iran's most highly enriched uranium was stored in an underground tunnel complex at its nuclear site in Isfahan prior to last year's U.S. strikes, the International Atomic Energy Agency said in a confidential report circulated to member states on Friday, marking the first time the U.N. nuclear watchdog has specified where uranium enriched to up to 60% purity has been kept.[1][2]

The disclosure adds a new dimension to the standoff over Tehran's nuclear program, arriving as the United States and Iran pursue fragile diplomatic negotiations and Washington maintains a large military buildup across the Middle East.

items.title: Green Party wins first-ever UK by-election, pushing Labour to third

featured_image.name: UK Greens trounce far right in key election as Labour fall to ...

items.description: Hannah Spencer, a 34-year-old plumber and local councillor, has won the Gorton and Denton by-election in Greater Manchester, delivering a result that marks the first time in the Green Party's history that it has won a UK parliamentary by-election. The victory, declared in the early hours of Friday morning, saw Spencer capture 14,980 votes — roughly 40.7% of the total — overturning a Labour majority of more than 13,000 from the 2024 general election. The result pushes Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party into third place in a seat the party had held for nearly a century.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: OpenAI raises record $110B from Amazon, Nvidia, SoftBank

featured_image.name: OpenAI said to be finalizing $100 billion funding round

items.description:
OpenAI announced on Friday a $110 billion funding round at a $730 billion pre-money valuation, the largest private financing deal ever recorded. The round includes $50 billion from Amazon, $30 billion from Nvidia, and $30 billion from SoftBank, with additional financial investors expected to join as the round progresses.[1]

The deal cements a sweeping strategic partnership between OpenAI and Amazon and deepens the AI company's ties to its largest chip supplier, Nvidia, while more than doubling the $40 billion OpenAI raised in March 2025 in what was then the biggest private tech fundraise on record.[2]

items.title: Chinese scientists set world records for kesterite, polymer solar cells

featured_image.name: Kesterite solar cells get ready to shine

items.description:
Researchers in China have announced back-to-back breakthroughs in solar cell technology, setting world records for both kesterite and polymer photovoltaic devices in findings published this week.

The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) reported that its Qingdao Institute of Bioenergy and Bioprocess Technology fabricated a kesterite solar cell achieving a power conversion efficiency of 15.45%, with a certified efficiency of 15.04%, according to pv magazine. Separately, a team at Wuhan University of Technology unveiled a polymer solar cell reaching 19.1% efficiency while retaining 97% of its performance after 2,000 hours of operation in air.[1][2]

items.title: Astronomers reveal trio of rare cosmic finds in single week

featured_image.name: Astrophotographers show the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A

items.description: In a burst of discoveries announced over the past week, astronomers using some of the world's most advanced telescopes have revealed three rare and violent cosmic phenomena: the first image of a young Sun-like star inflating a protective bubble in space, possible evidence of an elusive black hole shredding a white dwarf, and the fading radio echo of a powerful explosion whose original blast went unseen.

items.title: Zelenskyy says he's ready to meet Putin for peace talks

featured_image.name: Zelenskyy speaks with Trump about peace efforts, eyes leaders ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he is ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin face-to-face to resolve the most difficult issues standing in the way of peace, while warning that surrendering Ukrainian-held fortress cities in the east remains a firm red line.

In a wide-ranging interview with Sky News published on February 27, Zelenskyy said there is a closing window to end the war — one tied to American domestic politics. "Now I think that we have a chance," he told correspondent Alex Rossi. "If it will be possible to achieve a peace, we will have, now we have this window" — between now and the U.S. midterm elections in November.[1][2]

items.title: Chinese scientists achieve 700 Wh/kg lithium battery breakthrough

featured_image.name: New breakthrough in lithium battery technology enables 700 ...

items.description:
A team of Chinese researchers has developed a novel lithium battery electrolyte system that achieves an energy density of 700 watt-hours per kilogram at room temperature — more than double the capacity of the best commercially available lithium-ion batteries. The findings, published February 25 in Nature, represent a potential leap forward for electric vehicles, aerospace, and cold-weather energy storage.[1][2][3]

The research was led by Professor Zhao Qing from the College of Chemistry at Nankai University, Academician Chen Jun, the university's executive vice president, and Researcher Li Yong from the Shanghai Institute of Space Power-Sources. Their approach replaces the conventional carbonate ester solvents used in commercial lithium battery electrolytes with a series of fluorinated hydrocarbon solvent molecules, establishing a lithium-fluorine coordination system in place of the traditional lithium-oxygen mechanism.[4][2]

items.title: Canada's Carney arrives in India to reset ties after diplomatic crisis

featured_image.name: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney visits India to restore ...

items.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in Mumbai on Friday, launching a four-day visit to India that marks his first official trip to the country since taking office and signals a diplomatic reset after years of strained ties between Ottawa and New Delhi.

items.title: Oil slides as U.S. and Iran extend nuclear talks

featured_image.name: U.S. and Iran wrap up 'most intense' nuclear talks with no deal - CNBC

items.description: Gold prices held firm near recent highs on Friday while oil slipped toward a weekly loss after the United States and Iran wrapped up their third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva without a deal but with a commitment to keep talking. The extension of diplomacy eased fears of an imminent military confrontation that could disrupt Middle Eastern energy supplies, pulling crude lower even as bullion remained supported by broader safe-haven demand.

items.title: ESA releases first image of comet 3I/ATLAS from its Jupiter-bound spacecraft

featured_image.name: What's the latest on 3I/ATLAS? Interstellar comet to exit solar system

items.description: Eight months after its discovery electrified astronomers worldwide, interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS is speeding away from the inner solar system, leaving behind a trail of scientific revelations about the chemistry of deep space. The ancient visitor — only the third object ever confirmed to have arrived from beyond our solar system — is now headed toward a close pass of Jupiter next month before vanishing into the interstellar void forever.

items.title: Asian shares fall as Nvidia slump and Pakistan-Afghanistan war rattle markets

featured_image.name: Asian stocks to ebb as Nvidia decline dulls mood

items.description: Asian markets fell on Friday as concerns over technology company valuations and a string of geopolitical flashpoints drove investors toward safe-haven assets, extending the cautious tone set by Wall Street's overnight decline. The yen and U.S. Treasuries strengthened, while gold held steady near elevated levels.

items.title: Nvidia drops sharply despite record earnings as Block cuts half its staff

featured_image.name: Nvidia (NVDA) earnings report Q4 2026 - CNBC

items.description:
Nvidia erased roughly $260 billion in market value on Thursday despite delivering another blockbuster quarter, dragging the Nasdaq Composite to its sharpest decline in weeks and unsettling global investors already on edge over the durability of the AI boom. Separately, fintech firm Block announced it would eliminate more than 4,000 jobs — nearly half its workforce — in what its co-founder Jack Dorsey called a structural shift driven by artificial intelligence.

The two developments, arriving on the same trading day, underscored a growing tension in markets: companies at the center of the AI revolution are posting record results, yet investors are demanding ever more proof that the spending frenzy will translate into lasting profits.

items.title: Nintendo plans $1.9B share sale as banks unwind stakes

featured_image.name: Nintendo plans around $1.9 billion share sale by Kyoto bank ...

items.description:
Nintendo is preparing for a roughly $1.9 billion share sale as major lenders including MUFG Bank and the Bank of Kyoto move to offload their strategic stakes in the "Super Mario" maker, Reuters first reported on Thursday, citing three people familiar with the matter.[1][2]

The disposal is expected to amount to about 300 billion yen, and a decision could come as early as Friday. The Kyoto-based gaming company is also planning a share buyback to help absorb the supply, the sources said. Nintendo did not respond to a request for comment.[2][3][4][1]

items.title: Pakistan declares 'open war' on Afghanistan after deadly border clashes

featured_image.name: Kabul hit after clashes on Afghanistan-Pakistan border

items.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan plunged into their most dangerous military confrontation in years as the Taliban launched a large-scale ground offensive against Pakistani positions along the disputed Durand Line on Thursday evening, prompting Pakistani airstrikes on Kabul, Kandahar, and Paktia province hours later. Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif declared "open war" against Afghanistan on Friday, posting on X: "Our patience has reached its limit. Now it is open war between us and you."[1][2][3]

The rapidly escalating conflict, unfolding during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, has shattered a fragile ceasefire brokered by Qatar last October and drawn the nuclear-armed neighbors into their most direct military engagement since the Taliban seized power in 2021.

items.title: Germany votes to let military intercept drones

featured_image.name: Germany expands military powers to fight drones | Reuters

items.description:
Germany's parliament on Thursday voted to expand the military's authority to intercept or shoot down drones, responding to a surge in unidentified aerial activity that officials have linked to Russia's hybrid warfare campaign against Europe.[1]

The Bundestag approved an amendment to the country's air security law with support from the governing conservatives, the Social Democrats, and the far-right Alternative for Germany opposition, according to Reuters. The legislation marks the culmination of months of political urgency over rogue drones spotted near airports, military bases, and critical infrastructure across the country.[1]

items.title: Venezuela suspends 19 Maduro-era oil contracts

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Venezuela suspends 19 oil, gas production-sharing ...

items.description:
Venezuela's oil ministry has suspended 19 oil production-sharing contracts with private companies that were signed under the administration of former President Nicolás Maduro, according to four sources with knowledge of the move who spoke to Reuters.[1]

The suspension has had no impact on the country's oil and gas output so far, the sources said. State oil company PDVSA continues to sell crude produced under the contracts while they are under review. Both the Venezuelan and U.S. governments are now scrutinizing the credentials of the firms involved and may recommend revoking some of the agreements.[2][1]

items.title: US and Congo sign $1.2B health deal amid African data-sharing concerns

featured_image.name: Democratic Republic of Congo and US agree $1.2 billion ...

items.description:
The United States and the Democratic Republic of Congo on Thursday signed a $1.2 billion health partnership, making the DRC the 19th country to enter a bilateral health agreement under the Trump administration's "America First Global Health Strategy."[1][2]

The five-year memorandum of understanding, spanning 2026 to 2031, includes up to $900 million in U.S. government assistance and a commitment from the Congolese government to increase its domestic health spending by $300 million over the same period, according to a joint statement from the two governments.[3][1]

items.title: Maduro asks judge to toss drug indictment over blocked legal fees

featured_image.name: US says it has not offered Maduro amnesty since election ...

items.description:
Lawyers for ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro filed a motion on Thursday in Manhattan federal court asking a judge to dismiss the indictment against him, arguing that the U.S. government has unconstitutionally blocked Venezuelan funds from paying his legal costs in violation of his Sixth Amendment right to counsel.

Attorney Barry Pollack submitted the filing in the Southern District of New York, asserting that the Trump administration's refusal to allow the Venezuelan government to cover Maduro's defense amounts to a due process violation that would render any trial "constitutionally defective," according to the Associated Press.[1]

items.title: Syria, Druze factions complete first prisoner swap since summer clashes

featured_image.name: Syrian government forces and Druze fighters exchange prisoners ...

items.description: The Syrian government and Druze factions controlling the southern city of Sweida carried out their first prisoner exchange on Thursday since deadly sectarian clashes erupted last summer, according to the Syrian government's Sweida media office. The swap marks a rare step toward a political resolution in one of the last regions of the country still outside Damascus's control.[1][2]

items.title: 171 bodies found in mass graves near Congo's Uvira after M23 withdrawal

featured_image.name: DRC fighting forces 200,000 people to flee as M23 advances, dozens killed

items.description: Congolese authorities on Thursday announced the discovery of two mass graves containing at least 171 bodies on the outskirts of the eastern city of Uvira, in an area the M23 rebel group recently vacated. The grim find underscores the toll of escalating violence in the region, which has persisted despite a U.S.-brokered peace deal between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda.
